relatedCi.source: Workflow conclusions independently queried by ci_repair; job conclusions and watched steps supplied from audio_sync's final GitHub API observations.

independentVisualReview.method: Read-only opening of the original PNGs
independentVisualReview.result: No blocking visible defect in the 18 reviewed images.
findings: All three rigs remain complete inside each final detail, with visible heads, limbs, weapons and feet on the same ground; Ka’rhek and Sa’keth remain distinct.
No terminal overlay or character clipping was visible in the final details.
In atmosphere, the hull remains identifiable but clearly attenuated with a thin contour and no visible mask rectangle.
During cloak release the hull returns, and it is opaque before ground contact.
No capsule or crash VFX were visible in the inspected ship images.
limits: Still PNGs do not prove temporal refraction, motion smoothness or audio.
Final images are native-scale details; full-scene walking context was captured earlier.
The native handoff Canvas is substantially obscured by the arrival message, so it does not provide a complete visual proof of all three ground supports.
This is not a global canonical 1:1 art qualification.

additionalConfirmation.method: Read-only opening of the original PNGs
additionalConfirmation.findings: The two final details show all three silhouettes and feet without the terminal panel; the three desktop optical phases were also inspected.
additionalConfirmation.scope: A subset of the same 18 images, not additional unique screenshots.

limits: The publication remains 15 successful workflows and 2 failed workflows; later QA candidates do not change these conclusions.
The six final trio images are native-scale details with earlier full-scene walking context. PNG timing and later full geometry reads are separate evidence.
Still-image review does not prove temporal refraction, motion smoothness or audio.
The native handoff Canvas is largely covered by the arrival message and is not a complete visual proof of all three ground supports.
No global canonical 1:1 art qualification is claimed.
